correctness.rationale: At testing level \(s\), an adversarial proxy chooses the bin giving the larger activation probability among bins whose scaled threshold contains the realized \(P\). This produces the decreasing envelope \(g_s(p)=h_2\) for \(p\le s/b_2\), \(h_1\) for \(s/b_2<p\le s/b_1\), and zero afterward, with thresholds capped at one. Since every valid null p-value stochastically dominates Uniform\([0,1]\), the worst expectation is the uniform integral \(W(s)=h_1\min(1,s/b_1)+(h_2-h_1)\min(1,s/b_2)\). Piecewise inspection shows \(W(s)\le s\) for every \(s\) exactly when the displayed coefficient is at most one. Necessity is attained by a uniform \(P\) and a deterministic proxy-bin selection realizing the envelope for sufficiently small \(s\). A fresh randomized grid replay found exact agreement between the criterion and the envelope test in 5000 parameter draws; this is supplementary to the analytic proof.
correctness.risk: The theorem is specific to two ordered bins and this particular nonquery-one active rule.

final_claim: For the two-bin active p-value rule that, in proxy bin \(J=i\), reports \(b_iP\) with probability \(h_i\) and otherwise reports one, where \(0\le h_1\le h_2\le1\), \(0<b_1\le b_2\le1\), and the proxy may depend arbitrarily on a valid null p-value \(P\), universal superuniformity holds exactly when \(h_1/b_1+(h_2-h_1)/b_2\le1\).
limitations: The auxiliary randomizer is independent, while the proxy bin may depend arbitrarily on \(P\).
Parameters are ordered as stated; no multi-bin extension is claimed.
